topic: Chronological Milestones of Grassroots Environmental Movements in India
questionText:

(I) Amrita Devi Bishnoi leads 363 martyrs sacrificing their lives to save sacred Khejri trees in Rajasthan (1730)

(III) Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad (KSSP) mobilizes the Silent Valley Movement to protect evergreen rainforests from a hydroelectric dam (1970s)
(IV) Medha Patkar and Baba Amte launch the Narmada Bachao Andolan opposing submergence by the Sardar Sarovar Dam (1985)

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Movement chronology: Bishnoi sacrifice (1730), Chipko movement (1973), Silent Valley struggle (late 1970s), and Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985 onwards).
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

topic: Water Vapor as Most Abundant Greenhouse Gas
questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Water vapor (H2O) is the single most abundant greenhouse gas contributing to the natural greenhouse effect on Earth.
Reason (R): However, anthropogenic climate change is driven primarily by Carbon Dioxide (CO2) and Methane because their atmospheric lifetimes are long and their concentrations are directly controlled by human emissions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed Reason explains Assertion without establishing causal mechanism.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to notice that Reason does not causally explain the Assertion.

options.text: (A) is true but (R) is false
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Assertion is true but Reason contains a factual error.

options.text: (A) is false but (R) is true
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to identify the scientific fallacy in the Assertion.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A). Water vapor has a brief atmospheric residence time (~9 days) acting as an amplifying feedback, whereas CO2 persists for centuries.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (C) is the correct choice.

topic: Kyoto Protocol Flexibility Mechanisms
questionText:
Match the Kyoto Protocol market mechanism in List I with its operational definition in List II:

List I:
(A) Clean Development Mechanism (CDM)
(B) Joint Implementation (JI)
(C) International Emissions Trading (IET)
(D) Certified Emission Reduction (CER)

List II:
(I) Annex I country invests in emission reduction projects in a Non-Annex I developing country (Article 12)
(II) Annex I country invests in emission reduction projects in another Annex I country (Article 6)
(III) Trading of assigned amount units (AAUs) between Annex I countries with emissions targets (Article 17)
(IV) Standard unit issued under CDM representing one metric ton of CO2 equivalent reduced or sequestered

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Kyoto Protocol Flexibility Mechanisms.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Kyoto Protocol Flexibility Mechanisms (International Relations and Environment):
CDM is developed-developing; JI is developed-developed; IET is cap-and-trade allowance trading; and a CER represents 1 metric ton of CO2 equivalent.
Hence Option D is correct.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

topic: Greenhouse Gases and Global Warming Potentials (GWP)
questionText:
Match the greenhouse gas in List I with its approximate 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP) relative to CO2 in List II (IPCC AR6 benchmarks):

List I:
(A) Carbon Dioxide (CO2)
(B) Methane (CH4)
(C) Nitrous Oxide (N2O)
(D) Sulfur Hexafluoride (SF6)

List II:
(I) 1 (The universal baseline standard)
(II) 27 to 30 (approx. 28 times more heat-trapping per unit mass than CO2)
(III) 265 to 273 (approx. 270 times more heat-trapping than CO2)
(IV) 24,300 (one of the most potent synthetic greenhouse gases known)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
GWP benchmarks: CO2 = 1, CH4 ~ 28, N2O ~ 273, and synthetic SF6 (electrical insulator gas) = 24,300.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
